items.computation: The letter states a fixed calendar deadline directly: 'spätestens bis 06.08.2026'. This is consistent with 'innerhalb von 72 Stunden' counted from the document date 03.08.2026 (03.08 + 72h ≈ 06.08). No BGB period-counting or authority deemed-delivery rules apply here since this is a private, non-authority sender giving an explicit calendar date. Due date taken as printed: 2026-08-06.

warnings: This letter shows strong hallmarks of a fake/predatory debt-collection scam: a Cyprus-registered 'Inkasso' firm chasing an alleged telephone-sold lottery/gambling subscription, with payment demanded to a private individual's account (Kontoinhaber A. Petrauskas) at a Lithuanian bank (IBAN LT71 7300 0101 2345 6789) rather than to the named creditor or the agency's own business account.

The extremely short 72-hour deadline combined with threats of immediate account seizure (Kontopfändung), a negative SCHUFA entry and criminal prosecution for 'Eingehungsbetrug' without any court judgment or Vollstreckungstitel is a classic high-pressure scam tactic; a private collection agency cannot lawfully seize a bank account or file a SCHUFA entry on its own authority.

The sentence 'Ein Widerspruch ist zwecklos und verursacht weitere Kosten' is itself a red flag: consumers always retain the right to dispute a claimed debt, and no legitimate creditor or collector discourages this or claims an objection is pointless.

No evidence of the underlying contract (date of the phone call, terms, recording reference) is provided despite the claim that it was 'telefonisch abgeschlossen'; do not pay or share bank/personal details, and verify independently (e.g. via consumer protection advice, Verbraucherzentrale) before taking any action.
The IBAN itself passes a formal checksum check, but that only confirms it is well-formed, not that the payee is legitimate or connected to any real creditor.
